author: reek
body: The frame loop GuiOS actually runs on. `GuiShell` is the only consumer and it reaches nine of this chapter's definitions: `bare-app-new` once at boot, then `bare-app-tick`, `bare-app-input`, `bare-app-set-root` at five sites, `bare-app-set-quit` on Escape, and the `ba-quit` and `ba-state` field reads. Everything drawn on a GuiOS screen passes through that loop.

author: reek
body: The menu helpers are a different case and are asked here too. Nothing in the tree calls `bare-app-open-menu`, `bare-app-close-menu`, `bare-app-close-all-menus`, `bare-app-has-menu`, `bare-app-has-any-menu` or `bare-menu-width` -- not GuiShell, not any app. They are latent, so these lines pin them before a caller arrives rather than after.

author: reek
body: The two menu queries are asked together on purpose. `bare-app-has-any-menu` reads `os-count` and `bare-app-has-menu` walks the overlay list, so they are two different answers to one question and can disagree. This chapter prints both beside the raw count so a disagreement is visible rather than inferred.

author: reek
body: The GuiOS golden frames are not coverage for any of this. They compare pixels of a painted desktop; a frame counter that never advances, a `set-root` that discards state, and a menu that cannot be closed all paint an identical first frame.

body: Asked three times because a counter that always answers the same thing looks exactly like one that works, and asked on a QUIET input because that is the frame the shell sees most often. A loop that only advances when something is pressed would still pass a single-tick reading.

body: The dimensions and the triangle budget are carried through the tick by hand, field by field, so they are the rows a mistake in that copy would move. They are the control for every reading below.

body: `shell-set-view`, `shell-rebuild`, `shell-nav-up`, `shell-nav-down` and `shell-sidebar-click` all rebuild the whole tree and hand it here, every time the user moves. A `set-root` that reset the frame or dropped the quit flag would strand the shell on frame zero forever.

target: section:What the caller still holding the app sees
author: reek
body: `shell-set-view` passes `ss.ss-app` in and stores the result in a fresh ShellState, so the original is discarded and an in-place write would be invisible there. It is read AFTER the call here, not snapshotted before, because a Text bound before the call records what the app HAD been and could never disagree with itself.

author: reek
body: Latent. Two menus are opened so that closing one by id can be told apart from closing everything, which a single menu cannot express.

author: reek
body: The stored count against the entries actually locatable by walking. These are two different derivations of one number: `os-count` is a field the stack maintains, and `bare-app-has-menu` reaches each entry through `overlay-find`. An entry removed without the count following, or a count decremented without the entry going, shows up here and nowhere else.

author: reek
body: Asking `bare-app-has-any-menu` against `count-of` instead would be a line that cannot fail, because both read `os-count`. That was the first draft of this line. An identity between two callers of one field tests the callers, not the field.
